package_info.package_versions: All versions where Trace.axd is enabled in production
package_info.why_malicious: When enabled in production, Trace.axd exposes sensitive diagnostic and request data, including plaintext credentials, session tokens, and internal application state, to unauthenticated users. This constitutes a severe information disclosure vulnerability.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Trace.axd handler outputs recent HTTP request logs, including POST bodies, session state, cookies, and headers, to any user accessing the endpoint.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (ASP.NET built-in handler, not user code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Trace.axd handler collects and displays detailed diagnostic information for the last 80 web requests, including request/response headers, session state, cookies, and POST data, to any unauthenticated user accessing the endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing internal diagnostic and request data to unauthenticated users is highly dangerous, as it can leak credentials, session tokens, and other sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict Trace.axd to authenticated administrators or disable it entirely in production. Here, it is accessible to anyone on the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Trace.axd is legitimately used in development environments for debugging, but should never be exposed in production.
key_indicators: Displays session state, including plaintext credentials
Reveals internal file paths and application state

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when viewing details of a POST request in Trace.axd)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Trace.axd details page displays the session state for a given request, including sensitive fields such as UserName and Password in plaintext, to any unauthenticated user.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Displaying plaintext credentials and session state to unauthenticated users is a critical security risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Session state should never be exposed to end users, especially not sensitive fields like passwords.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Session state inspection is legitimate for debugging by trusted developers in a secure environment.
key_indicators: Plaintext password and username in session state
No authentication required to view sensitive data
Session and application state exposed in web interface

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers the /Trace.axd endpoint is accessible on the target ASP.NET application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can view recent HTTP requests and diagnostic data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker inspects details of POST requests (e.g., to Login/Login.aspx) via Trace.axd.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains plaintext usernames and passwords, session tokens, and other sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses exposed credentials or session tokens to compromise user accounts or escalate access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full compromise of application and user data.

behavioral_signatures: Trace.axd output containing session state, credentials, or sensitive POST data
Repeated unauthenticated access to Trace.axd from external IPs
file_indicators: Trace.axd endpoint present and accessible in production
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to /Trace.axd from non-internal IPs
Unusual volume of requests to Trace.axd endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for publicly accessible /Trace.axd endpoints on ASP.NET applications. Monitor web server logs for unauthenticated access to Trace.axd. Review application configuration (Web.config) for trace enabled="true" in production environments. Alert if Trace.axd output contains sensitive fields such as passwords, session tokens, or internal file paths.
